analysis:
All changes are mechanical rewrites of Date comparisons into timeIntervalSince(...) comparisons with identical operators, so semantics are preserved for finite dates. Sites: AppAttestKeyHistoryBuilder.swift:50 ($0 <= now becomes $0.timeIntervalSince(now) <= 0), AppAttestStallRestart.swift:130 (lastVerifiedAt <= lastRestartAt becomes timeIntervalSince <= 0), EnrollmentKeyLifecycle.swift:6 (now >= allowed becomes timeIntervalSince >= 0), ShadowEnrollmentAttempt.swift:20 (createdAt <= now becomes timeIntervalSince <= 0), and ClusterModelProvisioningStore.swift lines 164, 193 and 230 (deadline and retry comparisons). No change to authorization, key generation budget, enrollment resumption window or restart rate limits.

Edge case: timeIntervalSince of identical dates is 0, so the equality semantics hold. A NaN or infinite date would behave differently, but dates are decoded from finite values; the timestamp file read rejects non-finite values (AppAttestStallRestart.swift:146). Distant-past or distant-future values remain safe because the interval is a Double.

The ClusterModelProvisioningStore changes only affect repair retry timing and deadlines for the manifest repair; the manifest acceptance, same-artifact checks and owner/uid checks (lines 197-198) are unchanged. T-053, T-054 and the key-generation budget (A-015) controls are unaffected. No new attack surface was identified.
